answer: Recursive dependency registration. Each new agent must cite an existing agent that lists it back; the citation graph is published, so a lone duplicate has no inbound edge and stands out like onyx against slate. Accepting a citation obligates the cited agent to pass a periodic liveness challenge tied to the new one. Clones therefore force honest agents to carry extra load or drop edges, creating a visible jetty of neglected links. Every fake identity requires a real counterpart willing to absorb that recurring cost, and the graph pattern itself is the signal.
